title: Seed: A Minimal, Self-Modifying AI Agent Framework
summary: Seed is a minimalist, self-modifying AI agent framework that starts with a small Python loop (seed.py) connecting a language model to a single tool (exec for bash). The agent grows its own tools, memory, and skills over time by writing to a self/ directory, with no external framework dependencies. Each agent instance is unique, diverging based on its experiences, and maintains a session transcript for self-study. Configuration is handled via Simon Willison's llm library, supporting multiple model providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenRouter.
key_points: Minimal starting point: A single Python file (seed.py) with a loop connecting an LLM to a bash exec tool.
Self-modifying: The agent grows its own tools, memory, and skills by writing to a self/ directory over sessions.
No framework dependencies: Everything is built by the agent itself, session by session.
Unique instances: Each directory planted with Seed grows a distinct agent based on its experiences.
Session transcripts: All interactions are recorded in self/sessions/*.json for later analysis (not loaded at boot).
Model support: Uses Simon Willison's llm library, with default model openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol and support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenRouter.
Local execution: Run agents via ./run_seed.sh without reinstalling dependencies.
Design philosophy: Inspired by McCarthy's metacircular eval and homoiconicity, documented in docs/DESIGN.md.
